fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but no. Luke says Jesus was met by ten lepers, and then he tells us they stood at a distance (Luke 17:12). So the meeting happens, just from way over there. It's like greeting a neighbor from the far end of the street, where everybody's waving and nobody's close enough to shake a hand.

Right on, baker! Jesus tells them, "Go, show yourselves to the priests." (Luke 17:14). Notice He doesn't say come over here first. He gives them a direction, and that's it. I'd have wanted a map and a cookie for the road.

True, friend! Luke says, "…as they were on their way, they were cleansed." (Luke 17:14). They haven't reached the priests yet. The cleansing shows up mid-walk, like pulling a batch out of the oven and finding the timer still has minutes left.

Yes, friend! When he saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God (Luke 17:15). Everybody had been walking one way, and he turns around. That's a U-turn, and I bet there's a whole lot of joy behind it.
Not this time, friend. Luke says he came back, "…praising God in a loud voice." (Luke 17:15). So he's loud about it. No whisper in that praise.

That's what the ten did at the start, friend, but this man does something different. He fell facedown at Jesus' feet in thanksgiving (Luke 17:16). Facedown at His feet is about as close as you can get. The ten stood at a distance and raised their voices (Luke 17:12-13), and he ends up right there.
Yes, friend! Luke says, "…and he was a Samaritan." (Luke 17:16). Later Jesus calls him "this foreigner" (Luke 17:18). So the one who came back is the Samaritan.

Galilee does show up in this story, baker, since Jesus is passing between Samaria and Galilee (Luke 17:11). But Luke says of this man, "…and he was a Samaritan." (Luke 17:16). Jesus even calls him "this foreigner" (Luke 17:18). Good guess, just a different region.

Judean is a fair guess, friend, but Luke doesn't use it here. He says, "…and he was a Samaritan." (Luke 17:16). Jesus then calls him "this foreigner" (Luke 17:18). That's the detail Luke gives us about him.

Sacrifices isn't the word Jesus uses, friend. He says, "Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?" (Luke 17:18). Glory is what Jesus names. Sacrifices never come up in this story.

Faith, baker! Jesus tells him, "Rise and go; your faith has made you well!" (Luke 17:19). That's the last thing Jesus says to this man in the passage. He came back and fell facedown at Jesus' feet (Luke 17:15-16), and those are the words Jesus gives him.
